note: Passage 3703 (Pro 1:5-6). 'hear' upgraded seed-qualifier -> characteristic (listening/receptivity, an IB operation). 'saying' (melitsah, mis-tagged contempt) read as understand's target (qualifier). Two distinct 'wise' occurrences kept apart.

dims.v: the wise one — the person of settled competence who still learns
the wise disposition that hears and grows rather than resting
welded to hearing (shama) and increase in learning
the wise here is the LEARNER-wise (still hearing/increasing), distinct from 264844 the sages-whose-words-carry-wisdom. The book's paradox: the wise are those who keep receiving.
to hear — receptive listening that takes instruction in
listening so as to increase in learning
paired with the wise (its bearer) and the growth in learning it yields
read as a characteristic (not the seed's qualifier): shama = the receptive-listening operation, an IB act the study registers (Reg 213 listen). It is the means by which the wise increase.
the discerning one — the person of understanding
paired with the wise; parallel figure in the couplet
nabon (Niphal participle) = the settled discerning person, parallel to the wise; here he obtains guidance (tachbulot). Distinct from 264840 the ACT of understanding a proverb.
guidance — steering, the skill of direction (from the sailor's ropes)
the discerning person who obtains it
the good obtained by the discerning (264836)
tachbulot pictures navigation — the inner capacity to steer a course through life; a distinct good from wisdom-as-competence and knowledge-as-content.
to understand — to penetrate the sense of wise speech
discerning a proverb, a saying, the words of the wise and their riddles
the act that closes the purpose-chain: the aim of all the foregoing
the Hiphil ACT of understanding (vs 264836 the discerning PERSON): its objects are the forms of wise speech — proverb, saying, words of the wise, riddles.
the wise/sages — those whose words carry authority
the wise as the source of the words and riddles to be understood
paired with their words/riddles as their expression

distinct occurrence of chakam from 264832: here the wise are the AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE ('the words of the wise'), not the learner who hears. The difference is the finding — the wise both receive and transmit.
